channel.title: Deep Dive: Human Origins, Language & Religion
channel.itunes:author: Matthew S. Yorek
channel.itunes:summary: Merged human origins audio series exploring the evolution of spoken language, proto-writing, cuneiform, Big Gods, ritual cooperation, and sacred history.
channel.description: Merged human origins audio series exploring the evolution of spoken language, proto-writing, cuneiform, Big Gods, ritual cooperation, and sacred history.

image.title: Deep Dive: Human Origins, Language & Religion

item.title: The Eyes on the Wall — Bateson's Honesty-Box Coffee Experiment, Watching-Eyes Meta-Analyses & Replication Boundaries
item.description: Critical audit of the watching-eyes literature from Bateson et al. (2006) breakroom coffee honesty-box study to large-sample preregistered replications and meta-analyses.

item.title: What the Neighbors Could See — Credibility Enhancing Displays (CREDs), Public Ritual Observability & Cooperative Trust
item.description: Empirical and evolutionary analysis of observable religious behavior: how public ritual attendance, visible taboos, and Credibility Enhancing Displays (CREDs) solve the cultural transmission problem and shape inter-personal trust among neighbors.

item.title: The Family Beneath the Long Barrow — Early Neolithic Chambered Tomb Pedigrees, Five-Generation Kinship & Ancient DNA at Hazleton North
item.description: High-resolution ancient DNA kinship reconstruction of 35 individuals from the 5,700-year-old Hazleton North long barrow (Fowler et al. 2021): a five-generation extended family pedigree, patrilineal continuity, four reproductive women with shared male partners, and spatial mapping across north and south L-shaped chambers.

item.title: When the Metronome Stops — Behavioral Synchrony vs. Shared Intentionality, Fire-Walking Heart-Rate Coupling & Public-Goods Triads
item.description: Experimental dissection of collective ritual mechanics: Reddish, Fischer & Bulbulia's (2013) n = 82 triad foot-pedal experiments separating passive metronome synchrony from mutually adjusted shared intentionality, alongside Konvalinka et al.'s fire-walking heart-rate recurrence plots.

item.title: The Seal and the Crack — Mohenjo-daro Seal DK5175/143, Shang Oracle Bone Ping 0368 & What Ritual Surfaces Preserve
item.description: Comparative material epistemology of ancient religion: what an undeciphered Mohenjo-daro steatite stamp seal (DK5175/143) vs. a dated Late Shang pyro-osteomantic turtle plastron inscription (Ping 0368) can and cannot prove about supernatural agency and ritual rules.

item.title: A Jaw From the Missing Chapter — Paleoproteomics, Mandibular Morphology & Middle Pleistocene Hominin Lineages
item.description: Paleoanthropological and paleoproteomic investigation of a fossil hominin mandible where ancient DNA failed: enamel/dentine collagen peptide mass fingerprinting, morphometric geometry, and what a single bone can and cannot resolve.

item.title: The Blank Cell in the Big Gods Debate — Seshat Missing-Data Coding, Chronological Priors & Retraction Reanalysis
item.description: Epistemological and statistical dissection of the Seshat Big Gods controversy: how coding unknown historical cells as zeros shifted the inferred appearance of moralizing gods relative to social complexity, and why absence of evidence, documented absence, and first attestation are distinct.

item.title: The Commune That Outlasted Its Neighbors — 19th-Century Religious vs. Secular Communes, Costly Requirements & Survival Hazard Models
item.description: Quantitative survival analysis of 200 nineteenth-century U.S. communes (Sosis & Bressler 2003): how costly taboos and behavioral restrictions correlate with commune longevity differently in religious versus secular communities.

item.title: What the Ritual Cost — Extreme Rituals, Pain, Heart-Rate Synchrony & Prosocial Donation Experiments
item.description: Field experiments on high-ordeal vs. low-ordeal religious rituals (Xygalatas et al.; Konvalinka et al.): physiological arousal, pain ratings, spectator-performer heart-rate coupling, and anonymous charitable donations.

item.title: The Stranger in the Sharing Game — Cross-Cultural Random Allocation Games, Moralizing Gods & Impartial Rule Following
item.description: Methodological and statistical audit of cross-cultural Random Allocation Games (Purzycki et al.): how die-roll coin allocations measure impartial rule-following toward distant co-religionists and what the binomial model can and cannot prove.

item.title: When Maize Moved — Ancient Teosinte Introgression, Highland Adaptation & the Archaeological Dispersal of Corn
item.description: Archaeobotanical, paleogenomic, and isotopic reconstruction of maize domestication: Balsas teosinte divergence, Mexicana highland introgression, microbotanical phytolith/starch clocks, and dietary transitions across the Americas.

item.title: Nine Thousand Years at Oakhurst — Holocene Southern African Ancient Genomes, Deep Genetic Continuity & Later Stone Age Shifts
item.description: Ancient DNA time-transect from the Oakhurst rock shelter in southern Africa (Gretzinger et al. 2024; Jakobsson et al. 2026): 10,000 years of Holocene San-related genetic continuity followed by late-Holocene pastoralist and Iron Age gene flow.

item.title: When Polynesia Met South America — Pre-Columbian Sweet Potato Genetics, Rapa Nui Voyaging & Trans-Pacific Contact
item.description: Behind the Curtain Evidence Ledger & Longform Analysis (When Polynesia Met South America): specimen-bound diagnostic mechanics, assay boundaries, and real clinical/forensic case studies.

item.title: Proto-Writing, Tokens & True Script — Jiahu Symbols, Danube Notation, Near Eastern Calculi & Sumerian Cuneiform
item.description: Behind the Curtain Evidence Ledger & Longform Analysis (How Ancient Accountants Invented Writing): specimen-bound diagnostic mechanics, assay boundaries, and real clinical/forensic case studies.

item.title: First Cities & the Fertile Crescent — Urban Epistemology, Polycentric Domestication & Ancient Philology
item.description: Behind the Curtain Evidence Ledger & Longform Analysis (From Neanderthals to the First Alphabet): specimen-bound diagnostic mechanics, assay boundaries, and real clinical/forensic case studies.

item.title: Animal Signals, Orality & Silicon Minds — Evolutionary Syntax Boundaries, Pre-Literate Memory & Large Language Models
item.description: Behind the Curtain Evidence Ledger & Longform Analysis (How AI and Neural Implants Rewrite Language): specimen-bound diagnostic mechanics, assay boundaries, and real clinical/forensic case studies.

item.title: When Stroke Steals Words vs. Meaning — Broca's 'Tan,' Sign-Language Aphasia & Inner Silence
item.description: Traces Broca's 1861 autopsy of Leborgne (and 2007 3T MRI re-scanning), Salk Institute ASL stroke dissociations, corollary discharge, and anendophasia.

item.title: Julian Jaynes on Trial — Did Bronze Age Humans Hear Gods Before Inventing 'I'?
item.description: Puts Julian Jaynes's 1976 Bicameral Mind hypothesis on philological and neurobiological trial against Homeric Greek, Middle Kingdom papyri, and corollary-discharge fMRI.

item.title: The First Anatomists of Speech — 430,000-Yr Ear Bones, Neanderthal Hyoids & Shanidar Care
item.description: Reconstructs Middle Pleistocene speech acoustics from Sima de los Huesos ossicles (2–4 kHz), Kebara 2's hyoid, FOXP2, and Shanidar 1's decades of social survival.

item.title: Before the Brain Had a Name — Egyptian Hearts, Aristotle's Radiator & Herophilus
item.description: How humanity spent 2,000 years locating mind in the heart or diaphragm—from Edwin Smith's trauma papyrus to Aristotle, Herophilus in Alexandria, and Galen's laryngeal pig.

item.title: Wine-Dark Seas & Unspeakable Odors — How Language Shapes Color, Smell & Bedside Pain
item.description: From Gladstone's 1858 shock over Homer's color words and Berlin & Kay's hierarchy to Jahai abstract odor vocabulary and cross-cultural bedside pain ideophones.

item.title: Diagnosing the Dead — Can Ancient DNA & Modern Medicine Decode Cuneiform & Athens?
item.description: Stages the fierce debate between dental-pulp ancient DNA paleogenomics and medical historians warning against retrospective diagnostic anachronism.

item.title: Babylonian Neurology vs. Cos — Esagil-kin-apli's 1050 BCE Seizure Tablet & Hippocrates
item.description: Reads Neo-Babylonian Sakikkū Tablet XXVI (~1050 BCE) side-by-side with Hippocrates's On the Sacred Disease (~400 BCE): Jacksonian marches, auras, and post-ictal paresis.

item.title: Twenty-Seven Body Parts to Apothecary Grains — How Language Built Number & Dosing
item.description: Traces embodied human numeracy from Oksapmin 27-locus body counting and Paleolithic bone tallies to Sumerian bullae and life-or-death ancient apothecary metrology.
